test_case_specs.notes: New files load the modules by runtime import() through a variable specifier, so tsc stays quiet and each test fails on its own. All tui.json access uses a temp dir (persist/load take a dir argument; createSidebarGeometry takes configDir); nothing touches the real ~/.keryx. Tests are not committed; the orchestrator commits.

exports: createSidebarGeometry({ columns, configDir?, mode? }) -> { state(), setMode(m), cycle() -> new preferred mode, resize(columns), subscribe(l) -> unsubscribe }
sidebar-geometry.ts.semantics: state() = { mode (effective), preferred (stored), width }. Width: default 34 (SIDEBAR_WIDTH); wide min(68, floor(columns/2)) when columns >= 100, else effective default with preferred kept; rail 5. Subscribers fire only when mode or width changes. setMode/cycle persist the PREFERRED mode to <configDir>/tui.json key `sidebar`; resize never writes. With no `mode` option the constructor loads the persisted one. Load: any unknown/corrupt/missing value gives default, never throws. Persist: read-merge-write, keeps theme and unknown keys, tolerates a corrupt file.
sidebar-geometry.ts.theme.ts: persistThemeId must also become read-merge-write (keep sidebar and unknown keys; corrupt or non-object file -> start from {}).

api.shell-chrome.ts: ShellChromeOptions.sidebar?: { geometry, version?, asciiIcons? }. When present: pinned header Box `sb-header` between the sidebar's top edge and `sb-top`, holding Text `sb-title` ('keryx v<version>') and three buttons `sb-mode-default|wide|rail` (onMouseDown -> geometry.setMode; active one accented, inactive ones identical to each other). Rail: header collapses to a glyph (id sb-title kept) plus the `sb-mode-default` expand button. sidebar.width follows geometry.state().width; renderer resize calls geometry.resize(renderer.width); Ctrl+L calls geometry.cycle() unless overlayActive() (which includes modal sources, the dock, queue-nav) and does not reach the composer; applyTheme recolours the header.

exports: SIDEBAR_SECTION_IDS (all 34 former sections), SIDEBAR_SECTION_CARD: Record<sectionId, cardId>
mountSidebarCards(otui, renderer, parent, { geometry, snapshot: () => snapshot, onOpenCard(cardId), asciiIcons? }) -> { refresh(), destroy() }
openSidebarCard(otui, chrome, cardId, { snapshot, initialTab?, runCommand?(command) }) -> ModalHandle | undefined
sidebar-cards.ts.snapshot: { sections?: Record<sectionId,string>, approvalsPending?: number, hold?: string, updateAvailable?: string, reviewsNotReady?: number }
sidebar-cards.ts.card: { id, order, icon, asciiIcon, title, severity: 'normal'|'attention'|'error', badge?, tabs, lines(textWidth, mode), rail() -> { glyph, badge? } }. lines for default/wide: 3..5 lines each <= textWidth, lines[0] starts with the icon and holds the title and the badge; rail: exactly one line <= 3 cells starting with the glyph.
sidebar-cards.ts.tab: { id (= section id), label, command?: string, lines(width) -> full wrapped value }. Route tab command '/routing', Model tab '/model'.
sidebar-cards.ts.badges: approvals -> pending count (Remote); reviews not ready -> count (Reviews); hold -> Remote; update -> Session; hold/update badge glyph is the implementer's choice but <= 2 cells.
sidebar-cards.ts.slots: one Box `sb-card-<id>` per card, in order, never removed or re-created (same renderable across mode switches); click on the slot calls onOpenCard(id) in default, wide and rail.

api.modal-host.ts: With the sidebar widened, the panel must be >= MODAL_PANEL_MIN_WIDTH (72), inside the terminal, and not clipped; works when the sidebar is widened after the host was first created. Default-mode behaviour (panel clamped to main, flow 269 AC2) is unchanged.

assumptions: Wide threshold SIDEBAR_WIDE_MIN_COLUMNS is 100 (wide shows 50 columns at 100); the plan only says 'below the threshold' without a number.
Shortcut Ctrl+L: Ctrl+O (block nav), Ctrl+Q (queue nav) and Ctrl+C are taken, Ctrl+B/F/A/E/W/K/U/D are textarea bindings; Ctrl+L is free in the shell and in OpenTUI's textarea keymap.
The 'tools' row (Tools: N available) is not in the plan's table; it is placed under Policy.
Version update raises the Session card; hold and approvals raise Remote; a not-ready review raises Reviews (the plan names the signals, not the cards for update and review).
Rail width 5 leaves a 3-cell row for glyph + badge; the implementer may reduce padding in rail mode.
Card detail modal reuses existing inspectors through tab.command (runCommand) rather than re-mounting them inside the tab body; pinned by the Route to /routing test only.
The 80x24 smoke relies on the harness's first Ctrl+C raising the 'Press Ctrl+C again to exit' toast.
